blocks.text: England fast bowler Josh Tongue has been ruled out of the upcoming white-ball tour of Australia with a toe injury.
The 28-year-old suffered the injury in Pakistan last month and didn't take part in the final two games of that tri-series.
He will now return to the UK for further assessment and miss the one-day and T20 matches in Australia, which start with an ODI in Perth on 13 November.
Tongue, who has taken 46 wickets in 17 matches this year, is likely to be back for the three-match Test series in South Africa in December, with the squad set to be named next week.
The white-ball tour of Australia will mark the first time England have played down under since the 2025-26 Ashes demolition.
Coach Brendon McCullum had previously said he wanted a strong team for the ODI leg of the trip to Australia in the build-up to the World Cup in southern Africa next year.
The New Zealander also conceded he would have to rotate his squad for the T20 leg, given England's schedule in a busy winter of five separate overseas tours.
Adil Rashid took four wickets as England beat Western Australia by 92 runs in their one-day warm-up match in Perth.
The 38-year-old was left out of the final three matches of the October tour of Pakistan and Sri Lanka but highlighted his importance down under, taking 4-35.
Fast bowler Jofra Archer chipped in with 3-34 as England ultimately cruised to victory.
It wasn't all straightforward though as a sloppy batting display saw England bowled out for 251.
Ben Duckett top scored with 49 while Liam Dawson was unbeaten for 44.
The hosts had England in trouble as they reached 60-1 before Rashid took a flurry of wickets, including Jayden Goodwin and Ashton Turner in successive deliveries.
Archer finished off the Western Australia tail, bowling them out for 159 and securing the win.
